title: Kernel bug playbook / quick triage (scratchpad)
content:
Context:
- Purpose: quick personal playbook & running log for triaging kernel-level regressions I hit while on rotation. Use this as a scratchpad to capture commands, small experiments, and what to escalate. Not polished.
- Recent incident summary (2025-02-13 evening): KV cache invalidates intermittently under bursty short-seq workloads; 99p token latency spikes ~2–3x for affected requests. Suspect eviction path + small-rw lock contention.

Quick triage checklist (one-page):
1) Reproduce locally with a small harness
   - start runtime with --kv-evict-debug and --trace-locks
   - replay recorded trace: tools/replay/short-seq-burst.json (recorded from prod cluster 02/13)
   - expected: steady 25ms p99; observed: spikes to 70–120ms every ~300–600 requests
2) Capture perf counters
   - commands:
     - perf record -g -p <pid> -o /tmp/perf.data
     - ./tools/kv-inspect --pid <pid> --hist > /tmp/kv-hist.log
3) Narrow to code paths
   - grep traces for "evict" and "rw-lock"
   - instrument around CandidateEvict::try_evict
4) Short-term mitigations
   - increase eviction batch size to reduce frequent wakes (config: kv.eviction.batch=64 -> 256)
   - enable conservative backoff for client library to smooth bursts
5) Escalate if reproducible across >1 host
   - open JIRA with reproduction steps, perf dump, and a minimal trace; tag eng-sre and platform-engineering

Notes / hypotheses (ordered by confidence):
- H1 (high): Frequent synchronous evict cycles holding global lock due to small batch size + high churn from short sequences. Eviction path holds write lock to update free list -> block token-serving.
- H2 (medium): Memory allocator contention in hot patch path (tcmalloc arena thrash) when many short-lived KV entries created/dropped.
- H3 (low): Network reorder causing duplicate inserts and immediate evictions (unlikely but flagged by two traces with identical keys within 1ms).

Experiments to try (chronological log):
- 2025-02-14 09:10 — baseline replay on my laptop (4-core): reproduced p99 spikes. Captured trace.
- 2025-02-14 10:05 — changed kv.eviction.batch=256 locally: p99 spikes reduced by ~40% but still present. Note: throughput stayed nominal.
- 2025-02-14 11:22 — instrumented CandidateEvict::try_evict: added timing metrics and lock-hold histograms. Observed lock hold tail at ~8–14ms during spike windows.
- 2025-02-15 15:30 — tried switching allocator to jemalloc on dev box: no meaningful improvement. Suggests not allocator-dominant.
- 2025-02-16 09:00 — deployed config change kv.eviction.batch=256 to canary (2 nodes). Canary saw 30% drop in spike freq; one node still had occasional spikes.

Immediate TODOs (priority sorted):
- [ ] Add per-key churn metric to kv exporter (prometheus) — who: Priya — ETA 2025-02-18
- [x] Add lock-hold histogram metrics in CandidateEvict (done locally) — pushed PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/2157
- [ ] Run cluster-scale A/B with eviction.batch=512 vs 256 for two hours during low traffic window — coordinate with SRE (Diego) — target 2025-02-19 02:00 UTC
- [ ] If A/B still shows spikes, prototype async eviction worker decoupled from hot path — spike reduction target >= 50%
- [ ] Draft postmortem if can reproduce across >3 hosts — include mitigations and long-term plan

Helpful commands / snippets:
- start debug runtime: ./bazel-bin/runtime/server --config dev.yaml --kv-evict-debug --log-level=debug
- replay harness: ./tools/replay --trace recordings/short-seq-burst-20250213.json --rate 2000
- export metrics for timeframe: curl -s http://localhost:9090/metrics | grep kv_evict_lock_hold_ms_bucket
- lightweight tracer: RUST_LOG=kv=trace ./bazel-bin/runtime/server ... > /tmp/trace.log 2>&1 &

Pointers to code & artifacts:
- CandidateEvict: serving-runtime/kv/evict.rs (look at try_evict and pop_free_list)
- allocator bits: third_party/tcmalloc/ (search arena_create)
- reproducer: recordings/short-seq-burst-20250213.json (archived in infra-volume)
- recent PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/2157 (lock histogram + metrics)

Open questions / decisions to make:
- Q1: increase eviction.batch to 512 by default? Pros: fewer wake-ups + bigger amortization. Cons: potential longer pauses during large eviction. Need canary A/B.
- Q2: async eviction worker design trade-offs. Should worker perform bounded evictions per tick or drain fully? Lean towards bounded to avoid long pauses.
- Q3: telemetry: do we need per-tenant eviction metrics or per-key only? Per-tenant might help tie to customer impact.

Notes-to-self for oncall handoff:
- If paged for high p99: first check canary flags (kv.eviction.batch) and the per-node lock-hold histogram metric. If lock-hold > 5ms at 95p, flip canary config to batch=512 for the affected node group and notify SRE.
- Avoid restarting runtime during traffic peak. Try config flip + slow rollout.

Random micro-ideas (brain dump):
- Use a two-tier free-list: small fast-path free-list for hot keys that never require full eviction, fallback to heavy evict for cold churn.
- Consider sharded eviction locks per-hash-segment (reduce contention) — surgical change but high payoff if correctness simple.

References & links:
- Slack thread: https://redwood.slack.com/archives/G01234567/p1707889322001234
- JIRA: JIRA-RT-4123 (investigation), JIRA-RT-4189 (canary config run)

Last short log (today, 2025-02-17):
- 08:30 — merged PR for lock histograms (PR 2157); started canary with batch=256 across 4 nodes. Metrics look marginally better.
- 09:45 — Diego ran perf capture on canary node, transferring /tmp/perf.data to s3://redwood-debug/perf-20250217-canary-1
- 11:00 — pairing with Samira to sketch async eviction prototype. Action: mock API for eviction worker and failure modes.

If I leave this doc and come back: next steps if morning: check canary p99, grep lock histograms, start A/B plan ticket, sync with SRE for scheduled A/B window.

-- Priya
(quick scratchpad; prune and formalize into a postmortem or runbook later)
